mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a decrease in consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 2% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies benefit from increased production and efficiency.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months signals a potential for continued accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate low interest rates.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL was below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors interpret this as a sign of economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% each in the last month signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as both consumer and housing sectors show growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS increase > 1% each in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increased by more than 1% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation environment (CPIAUCSL > 4% for 3 consecutive months), a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a potential pivot in monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate easing financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% for 3 months and FEDFUNDS decrease
regime_hint: high inflation with potential monetary easing
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL was above 4% for three consecutive months and FEDFUNDS decreased.
